title: Culture and feedback on ways of working
blurb: Define culture, read persistent non-compliance as a warning sign, investigate resistance and act on feedback about how the project works.
question: Team members keep raising issues by message instead of the agreed issue form, saying the form takes twenty minutes. The project manager simplifies the form with them. Why is this a sound response?

teach.body: Formally, culture is the set of shared attitudes, values, goals and practices. In plain English: 'how things are really done round here'. Each organization in the organizational ecosystem brings its own culture, and a project culture emerges as the temporary team works together. Change succeeds when the agreed ways of working fit that culture, or when the culture is deliberately helped to evolve.

teach.caption: The project board is responsible for establishing clear feedback loops that support adapting and evolving the project.

teach.body: PRINCE2 asks projects to gather and act on feedback so that the defined ways of working stay aligned with how people actually work. Persistent non-compliance with project processes is often a leading indicator that the agreed ways of working no longer fit the emerging project culture. So the first question is 'why are people working around this?', not 'how do we enforce it harder?'

teach.caption: Illustrative. A rising trend of workarounds warns of misalignment before it damages control of the project.

teach.h: Responding to a process people bypass

root.label: A project process is persistently bypassed

children.label: Realign the way of working
children.sub: adapt it with the people who use it, then communicate

teach.body: Culture runs through the change itself. The evolving culture is one of the things to consider in the change management approach, and culture is one of the characteristics that can differ between the current, interim and target states. When a group resists, the resistance shows where communication should be focused: investigate the reasons rather than sidelining the group.

rows.label: Assumes
values: The fit may be the problem

teach.body: Brindle Foods is introducing a new production-scheduling system. Project manager Sofia Marin notices that, week after week, line supervisors report issues by message rather than on the agreed issue form. At a short feedback session they explain the form asks for data they do not have on the factory floor. Sofia redesigns it with them to a few key fields, project support still records each issue in the register, and form use recovers within a fortnight.

teach.text: When feedback leads to a simpler issue form, the reason for acting comes from the people element (keeping ways of working aligned with culture), not from the issues practice. And resistance is a signal to investigate, not a reason to exclude people from the project.

items: Culture: the set of shared attitudes, values, goals and practices (manual 3.2.3).
Gather and act on feedback so the defined ways of working match how people actually work.
Persistent non-compliance with project processes is often a leading indicator of misalignment with the emerging culture.
Pockets of resistance show where communication should be focused: investigate why.
The evolving culture is a consideration in the change management approach.

summary: You can now define culture, explain why persistent non-compliance is a leading indicator that ways of working no longer fit the emerging culture, and describe the right response: gather and act on feedback. You can also link culture to resistance and to the change management approach.

A.q: Which is the PRINCE2 definition of culture?
options: Instructing the execution of tasks in line with agreed ways of working
The set of shared attitudes, values, goals and practices
Motivating people to achieve the project's objectives
The ability to relate and work across different cultures
A.why: Culture is the set of shared attitudes, values, goals and practices (manual 3.2.3).

whyNot.0: Instructing the execution of tasks in line with agreed ways of working is the definition of management.
whyNot.2: Motivating people to achieve objectives is part of leadership.
whyNot.3: Relating and working across cultures is cultural intelligence.

A.q: What does PRINCE2 say persistent non-compliance with project processes often indicates?
options: The project is forecast to exceed its stage tolerances
The team managers need tighter work package tolerances
The agreed ways of working no longer fit the emerging culture
The project board should appoint a separate change authority
A.why: Persistent non-compliance is often a leading indicator that the agreed ways of working have become unaligned with the emerging project culture (manual 3.2.3).

whyNot.0: A forecast tolerance breach is about time, cost, scope and the other targets, not about people working around processes.
whyNot.1: Work package tolerances limit time, cost and scope for team managers; they do not address misfit with culture.
whyNot.3: A change authority approves requests for change; it does not address why people bypass processes.

A.q: Why should a project gather and act on feedback about its ways of working?
options: To keep defined ways of working aligned with how people actually work
To remove the need for the project board to arrange project assurance
To let the team change baselined products without any formal approval
To decide which team members should be moved off the project
A.why: Feedback is acted on so that the defined ways of working remain aligned with how people are actually working (manual 3.2.3).

whyNot.1: Project assurance remains a board responsibility; feedback on ways of working does not replace it.
whyNot.2: Changes to baselined products still go through change control in the issues practice.
whyNot.3: The purpose of feedback is alignment of ways of working, not selecting people to remove.

B.q:
Which two statements about culture are correct?
1. Culture is the set of shared attitudes, values, goals and practices.
2. Every organization in the organizational ecosystem shares the same culture.
3. Persistent non-compliance can signal misalignment with the project culture.
4. Feedback on ways of working is gathered once, at project closure.
options: 1 and 2
2 and 4
1 and 3
3 and 4
B.why: Statement 1 is the definition of culture and statement 3 reflects the guidance on non-compliance as a leading indicator.

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: each organization has its own culture.
whyNot.1: Both are false: cultures differ between organizations, and feedback is gathered and acted on throughout.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: feedback should be gathered and acted on as the project progresses.

B.q: Team members keep reporting issues by message instead of the agreed form, saying it takes twenty minutes. The project manager shortens the form with them. Why is this appropriate?
options: It means project support can stop maintaining the issue register
It allows the daily log to take over from the issue register
It moves decisions on issues from the board to team members
Feedback shows this way of working no longer fits how people work
B.why: Acting on feedback keeps defined ways of working aligned with how people actually work; persistent workarounds were the warning sign (manual 3.2.3).

whyNot.0: Project support still maintains the issue register; only the way issues are raised has been simplified.
whyNot.1: Formal issues still go in the issue register; the daily log is for informal issues.
whyNot.2: Decision authority on issues is set by the board and the issue management approach, and the form change does not alter it.

B.q: Which consideration for the change management approach relates most directly to culture?
options: The evolving culture
The risk appetite
The quality tolerance
The change budget
B.why: The evolving culture is one of the considerations when deciding the level of detail in the change management approach (manual 3.2.1).

whyNot.1: Risk appetite is the business's attitude to risk, used in the risk practice.
whyNot.2: Quality tolerance comes from acceptance criteria and quality specifications.
whyNot.3: The change budget funds approved changes to the baseline under the issues practice.

C.q: A user group openly criticizes a new process, and some staff quietly keep using the old one. What should the project manager do, and why?
options: Escalate to the board, as resistance is a forecast tolerance breach
Investigate the resistance, as it shows where to focus communication
Raise a request for change, as resistance proves the baseline is wrong
Take them off the stakeholder list, as resistance slows the delivery
C.why: Pockets of resistance indicate where communication should be focused; the project should find out why people resist and act on that feedback.

whyNot.0: Resistance is not in itself a forecast breach of stage or project tolerance.
whyNot.2: A request for change proposes a change to a baseline; resistance needs investigating before any such conclusion.
whyNot.3: Removing resistant people from engagement makes adoption less likely.

C.q: Which role is responsible for establishing clear feedback loops to support adapting and evolving the project?
options: Team manager
Project support
Business layer
Project board
C.why: Creating the right environment for success includes the project board establishing clear feedback loops to support adapting and evolving the project.

whyNot.0: Team managers manage their team's work and relationships; the board sets up the project's feedback loops.
whyNot.1: Project support provides administrative and planning services, not the project's feedback environment.
whyNot.2: The business layer commissions the project and sets project tolerances; it sits outside the project management team.

C.q: How does culture relate to the change management approach's 'characteristics for each state'?
options: Culture is recorded separately in the project's risk register
Culture is fixed, so it is left out of the state descriptions
Culture is one of the characteristics that can change between states
Culture is described in the communications schedule for each group
C.why: Characteristics for each state highlight what changes, for example routines, practices, processes, culture, responsibilities, structure and capabilities.

whyNot.0: The risk register holds specific risks, not a description of each state's culture.
whyNot.1: Culture can evolve, which is why the evolving culture is a consideration for the approach.
whyNot.3: The communications schedule sets out communication to each group, not the characteristics of each state.

reteach.title: The desire path across the grass
reteach.question: When people keep cutting across a lawn instead of using the paved path, what should the park manager learn?

blocks.body: A worn track across the grass shows where people actually want to walk. A manager can put up 'keep off' signs, but the track usually comes back. A wiser manager asks why, and often paves the desire path. Persistent non-compliance with a project process is the same signal: the agreed way of working no longer fits how people really work.

blocks.text: Realigning a way of working does not mean dropping control: the issue still gets recorded, the risk still gets assessed. The method is kept; the way people use it is made to fit.

explain.body: Culture is the set of shared attitudes, values, goals and practices. Each organization has its own, and a project culture emerges as the team works together.

test.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. Culture is the set of shared attitudes, values, goals and [?].
options: practices
tolerances
baselines
objectives
test.why: PRINCE2 defines culture as the set of shared attitudes, values, goals and practices (manual 3.2.3).

whyNot.1: Tolerances are permitted deviations set for plans, not part of the definition of culture.
whyNot.2: Baselines are approved product versions under change control.
whyNot.3: Objectives are what the project must achieve; 'goals' is already in the definition, and the missing word is practices.

explain.body: Gather and act on feedback so that the defined ways of working stay aligned with how people actually work. The board establishes clear feedback loops so the project can adapt and evolve.

test.q: A project manager notices a gap between the agreed ways of working and how people actually work. What does PRINCE2 recommend?
options: Record the gap as a risk for the next stage plan
Gather and act on feedback to realign them
Leave it for review in the end project report
Ask project assurance to enforce the process
test.why: PRINCE2 asks projects to gather and act on feedback so ways of working stay aligned with how people actually work.

whyNot.0: The gap already exists, so it is not an uncertain future event; and deferring action leaves the misalignment in place.
whyNot.2: Waiting until closure lets the misalignment persist through the project.
whyNot.3: Project assurance gives the board independent confidence; it is not an enforcement function for project processes.

explain.body: Persistent non-compliance with project processes is often a leading indicator: an early warning that the agreed ways of working have drifted away from the emerging project culture.

test.q: How does PRINCE2 describe persistent non-compliance with project processes?
options: A lagging measure of the benefits already realized
A trigger for the board to close the project early
A type of off-specification raised against products
A leading indicator of misaligned ways of working
test.why: It is often a leading indicator that the agreed ways of working have become unaligned with the emerging project culture.

whyNot.0: Benefits measures relate to the business case, not process compliance.
whyNot.1: Premature closure is a board decision when the project is no longer justified or viable.
whyNot.2: An off-specification is a product that will not meet its specification.

explain.body: Pockets of resistance show where communication should be focused. Investigate why people resist: their reasons are feedback the project can act on.

test.q: What do pockets of resistance indicate, according to PRINCE2?
options: Which people to move out of the project team
Which risks to transfer to the suppliers
Where communication should be focused
Where stage tolerances should be tightened
test.why: Pockets of resistance show where communication should be focused (manual 3.4).

whyNot.0: Resistance is a reason to engage people, not to move them out.
whyNot.1: Risk transfer is a risk response for uncertain events, not a response to resistance.
whyNot.3: Stage tolerances are set by the board for performance targets, not in response to resistance.
